source.version: Journal version of record: Human-Computer Interaction, DOI 10.1080/07370024.2026.2717534, published online 21 Sep 2026 (received 17 Jan 2026, revised 9 Jul 2026, accepted 3 Aug 2026). PDF includes a Taylor & Francis cover page, so PDF page = printed page + 1.
source.title_on_document: Dialogue patterns in human-AI co-creation: how interaction structure shapes output and process

supplement.where: No online supplement is referenced. Appendices A (system prompts), B (dialogue-act coding scheme), and C (coding validation) are inside this PDF, PDF pp. 30-32.
supplement.holds: Nothing beyond the main text for creativity outcomes. Per-arm originality and appropriateness means are shown only in Figure 4 (except IC and ALP appropriateness, given in text); Figure 7 prints pairwise Cohen's d for all contrasts; bootstrap CIs and Welch p-values behind Figure 7 are not printed.

paper_design_summary: US MTurk workers were randomly assigned to one of four interfaces built on the same model (Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite), each structuring AI help differently: human-lead expand (HLE), AI-lead propose (ALP), iterative critique (IC), and free dialogue (FD). Each person wrote a user persona and usage scenario for a gardening seed-trading app. Three blinded raters scored originality and appropriateness (summed into a composite creativity score); the paper also computes descriptive richness (adjective plus adverb share) and between-persona embedding similarity within each condition against a permutation null. There is no no-AI arm.

studies.label: Online experiment: four human-AI interaction patterns for persona creation

assignment.what_was_assigned: One of four AI interaction designs (HLE, ALP, IC, FD); all arms had generative AI
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one condition and completed a user persona creation task with AI assistance structured according to their assigned pattern.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Section 4.1; sequential balancing described same page; Figure 2, PDF p. 10
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Section 4.2: 'Substantial exclusions were applied based on pre-registered quality criteria'. No registry link or ID is given, and the paper does not say what else was preregistered.

arms.name: HLE (human-lead expand)
arms.description: Participant drafts; invokes AI via a menu of five expansion options (demographics, scenario ideas, goals, frustrations, personality); AI output appears in a separate panel and must be integrated manually.

arms.name: ALP (AI-lead propose)
arms.description: AI generates five persona concepts; participant picks one and develops it, with AI available in constrained follow-up chat that cannot edit the workspace.

arms.name: IC (iterative critique)
arms.description: Participant drafts independently and clicks 'Get Feedback' for structured AI critique (strengths, areas for improvement, recommendations); AI does not write drafts.

arms.name: FD (free dialogue)
arms.description: Split-pane: unconstrained chat with the AI beside the participant's workspace; AI can see but not edit the workspace.

participants.exclusions: 31 of 275 assigned participants excluded under pre-registered quality criteria: repeat submissions (same worker ID or IP; first valid kept), fewer than 3 logged interactions or under 3 minutes, and submissions flagged by RAs for bot-like, nonsensical, or inattentive content. Per-arm counts at assignment not given. Analysis is on the 244 retained (not ITT).
participants.who: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers, 99%+ HIT approval, at least 1000 prior HITs; mean age 38.1, 54% male (Table 1)
participants.quote: A total of 275 participants were initially assigned to one of four human–AI interaction patterns. After applying the predefined data quality criteria, 31 participants were excluded, resulting in a final sample of 244 participants.
participants.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 8), Section 4.2; arm ns in Figure 2 (PDF p. 10) and Table 1 (PDF p. 10, printed p. 9)

ai_tool.name_model: Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite (preview release 09/2025), via OpenRouter as google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-09-2025, condition-specific system prompts
ai_tool.how_used: Role differs by arm: HLE = on-demand menu expansions in a side panel (closest to suggestions); ALP = AI supplies five starting concepts then constrained chat (ideas_supplied); IC = structured critique of the participant's own draft (refinement); FD = free chat beside the workspace (open_chat). In no arm could the AI edit the workspace directly except that participants copied or typed content themselves.

task.description: Create a user persona (name, demographics, description) and a usage scenario for a mobile app that helps local gardeners trade seeds and produce. Persona-creation is a design task producing a narrative text artifact; coded creative_writing, could also be read as other.
task.duration: Advertised as 20-40 minutes; mean task duration 10:13 (min:sec), Table 1

outcomes.name: Composite creativity score (originality + appropriateness, 0-20)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Sum of originality and appropriateness ratings (each 10-point), each the mean of three independent blinded external judges 'with backgrounds relevant to evaluating narrative artifacts (e.g., creative writing)'. ICC(3,3) = .84, 95% CI [.80, .87]. Convergent check with Qwen3-32B LLM ratings (overall creativity r_s = .71), reported pooled only, not by condition.

contrasts.reported: Table 1: IC 17.57 (SD 2.31, n = 61) vs ALP 15.92 (SD 4.04, n = 62). Games-Howell: mean difference = 1.64, p = .033, 95% CI [.096, 3.191]. Figure 7 cell 'ALP vs IC', Creativity (composite): d = -0.50* (survives Holm across 6 pairs). Omnibus Brown-Forsythe F(3, 199.14) = 2.88, p = .0437, eta^2 = .035, 95% CI [.000, .081].

outcomes.name: Between-persona semantic similarity within condition (vs permutation null)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Cosine similarity for every pair of personas, computed separately for persona content, scenario content, and concatenated persona-plus-scenario text, with two embedding models (6 cells). Each condition's within-condition mean pairwise similarity is compared to a 10,000-shuffle permutation null of condition labels. Robustness: length-controlled version projecting out the length-correlated embedding direction gives the same direction with larger z; uncontrolled values are the primary inference. 244 personas embedded.

contrasts.control_arm: Permutation null / between-condition baseline (all 244 personas, labels shuffled)
contrasts.reported: Higher similarity = lower diversity (sign reversed). Persona content: nomic-embed z = +2.59, p_holm = .037; jina-embeddings z = +2.79, p_holm = .019. Within-condition cosine similarity: nomic 0.718 vs between-condition baseline 0.695; jina 0.833 vs baseline 0.813. Combined text: nomic borderline p_holm = .056, jina p_holm = .032.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 21 (printed p. 20), Section 5.5; PDF p. 22 (printed p. 21), Figure 6

diversity_detail.metric: Within-condition mean pairwise cosine similarity, reported as z against a permutation null (paper also frames it as semantic distance = 1 - cosine similarity, following Anderson et al. 2024)
diversity_detail.embedding_model: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 and jina-embeddings-v2-base-en (both 8,192-token context; no persona truncated)
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of personas within a condition, separately for persona content, scenario content, and combined text
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Permutation test shuffling condition labels 10,000 times; two-sided p with Holm-Bonferroni correction across four conditions
diversity_detail.notes: No direct condition-versus-condition diversity test or effect size is reported; each arm is compared with chance. Per-cell distributions shown as violins in Figure 6.

data_and_code.data_url: Not public; available from the corresponding author on reasonable request (PDF p. 27, printed p. 26)

eligibility.reason: Individuals randomly assigned (PDF p. 9) to four generative-AI configurations, so all contrasts are ai_design; there is no no-AI arm. 244 people analyzed (275 assigned). Outcomes are blinded rater scores of originality, appropriateness, and composite creativity on the written persona, plus embedding diversity.

one_line_finding: Among 244 MTurk workers using four AI interaction designs, iterative critique produced higher composite creativity than AI-lead propose (17.57 vs 15.92 of 20, difference 1.64, p = .033; d = 0.50) and higher appropriateness, originality did not differ across conditions (F(3, 240) = 2.42, p = .084), and IC personas were more similar to each other than chance while ALP output was more diverse (PDF pp. 10, 16, 21, 23).
open_questions: No no-AI arm, so the paper speaks only to ai_design contrasts. Which pair is the primary record is not fixed by the paper: the highlighted contrast is IC vs ALP; under codebook rule 3, FD (free chat) is the arm closest to a general chatbot and could serve as the reference.
Rater type: 'blinded external judges with backgrounds relevant to evaluating narrative artifacts (e.g., creative writing)' coded expert_raters; could be read as human_raters.
Preregistration is mentioned only for exclusion criteria; no registry or link, and the composite is called 'the primary outcome measure' without saying it was preregistered as primary.
Task (user persona and scenario) coded creative_writing; it is a design-research artifact and could be coded other.
Diversity is tested per arm against a pooled permutation null, not between arms, so it does not give a direct treatment-control diversity contrast.
notes: Locators give the PDF page, then the printed journal page (PDF page = printed page + 1 because of the cover sheet). Outcomes not listed because they are self-reports or process measures, not scored on output: mental demand, trust, user control, perceived AI role, collective ownership (Table 2, Section 5.2), task duration, interaction count, artifact count, dialogue-act patterns and entropy (Section 5.3). Within-condition correlations of entropy and critique share with creativity (Section 5.3.2) and DR-creativity correlations are non-randomized and not listed. Baseline DAT (Divergent Association Task) was measured before the task and did not predict creativity (r_s = .026, p = .685; PDF p. 24); it is a covariate, not an outcome. Paper reports ~80% power for Cohen's f = .19 with N = 244 (PDF p. 15). Table 1 creativity means are described as 'the average score out of 20 of the three raters'.
